 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:-
That on 24-10-2021 at about 07.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding two-wheeler/Suzuki Access bearing No.KA-02-HT-1268 along with his wife Mamatha as pillion rider, proceeding from (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Mallappanahalli to Bengaluru, on NH-75 i.e., Kunigal- Nelamangala Road, they came in front of Mahadevapura Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time the driver of Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550 proceeding front to the petitioner was suddenly, reckless and negligently stopped the car in front of the petitioner's two-wheeler and consequent to which the petitioner's two-wheeler hit to the hind portion of the car and accident was occurred.

Due to terrific impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to VP Magnus hospital,
Nelamangala, wherein after first aid he was shifted to Citi hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has spent huge amount towards medical expenses,
conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 43 years and was working as employee in Kaviraj Cooker Factory, Luggere, Peenya, Bengaluru and drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries the petitioner is uanble to attend his duty and hence sustained loss of income.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Car involved in the accident and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Car.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Car, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550, but the original copy of the policy is in the Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98360407/
2 possession and control of the respondent No.1 and the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the said Car has no valid and effective driving licence and the owner allowed the driver to drove the same knowingfully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence and thereby there (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 is clear violation of policy terms and conditions.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of offending Car and petitioner being a rider of two-wheeler rode the same without wearing safety headgear and it is violation of M.V. Act.

The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 24.10.2021 at about 07.30 p.m, on NH-75 Road, Kunigal - Nelamangala Road, opposite to Mahadevapura Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-MD-2550 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03.
What Order or Award?

06. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined MRO as (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 PW.2 and through them got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed his side evidence.
The respondent No.2 got examined MRO as RW.1 and through him got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.
07. The learned counsels for petitioner and respondent No.2 have argued on main matter.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not advanced arguments, hence respondent No.1 arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:

sentences.text: 3 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of cross- examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that there is no document or appointment letter and (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 he has not given any resignation to his job but only intimate about the accident and his factory did not removed him from his job and admits that the offending car did not hit his vehicle from front side, his motor cycle hit against the back portion of car and admits that on the date of accident itself he knew which vehicle has caused accident and denied to the suggestion that the Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550 did not caused accident to him and that the bleeding injuries were healed.
10.
Further, MRO of Citi hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.2 and he he has produced MLC register, Case sheet and X-ray as per Ex.P.18 to 20.
During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that he do not know the contents of Ex.P.18 to 20 produced by him.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Nelamangala Traffic Police against the driver of the offending car.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Sketch.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which shows involvement of the offending car in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which indicates that (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.7 is Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending car for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing injuries to the petitioner.

Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary which indicates that petitioner was admitted to City hospital, Bengaluru, as inpatient from 25.10.2021 and discharged on 02.11.2021 for nearly 08 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.14 is Photographs.
Ex.P.15 is X-ray.
Ex. P.16 is scan film.
Ex.P.18 is MLC register.
Ex.P.19 is Case sheet and Ex.P.20 is X-ray.
12. Further, on behalf of the respondent No.2 MRO of VP Magnus hospital, Nelamangala, is examined as RW.1 and he he has produced Police intimation and MLC extract as per Ex.R.2 and 3.
During the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel he stated that the injured petitioner was shifted to other hospital after taking first aid treatment in their hospital.

13. On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has proved that he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 24-10-2021 at about 07.30 p.m, (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 on NH-75 Kunigal-Nelamangala Road, in front of Mahadevapura Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala Taluk, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing No.KA-41-MD-2550 by its driver, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98360407/
4

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 43 years and was working as employee in Kaviraj Cooker Factory,
Luggere, Peenya, Bengaluru and drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- p.m and has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.
Due to accidental injuries, he is uanble to attend his duty and hence sustained loss of income.
15. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.8 driving licence and Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said documents are not (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon, according to which, date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 10.06.1978.
The alleged accident occurred on 24.10.2021.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 43 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 43 years as on the date of accident.
16. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents or evidence or and no employer was examined before the tribunal.

17. In the case on hand the petitioner has not examined the doctor who examined him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he sustained any physical or functional disability and there is no evidence on record to show there is a loss of income or future income and loss of income during laid up period.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that he is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income and also loss of income during laid up period.
(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 18. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary, according to which he was admitted to Citi hospital as inpatient for 08 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

19. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per Ex.P.14 Photographs, Ex.P.15 and 20 X-rays, Ex.P.16 scan film, Ex.P.19 Case sheet, which indicates that on account of accidental injuries, the petitioner would have undergone pain and agony due to grievous injuries sustained.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.
20. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.11 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,42,893/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,42,893/- under the head of medical expenses.

Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98360407/
5 21.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
2 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  3.
Medical Expenses 2,42,893-00  Total 3,02,893-00 22.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,02,893/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

23. Regarding liability:- The respondent No.2 has taken several defences in its written statement,
but has not lead any evidence to prove its contention and to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Though, the respondent No.1 has appeared, but not filed written statement and not contested the case.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 4 admits issuance of policy in respect of offending Car and the same is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
But the respondent No.2 has not placed any material to show that the owner or driver of the offending car have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending car,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.3,02,893/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a to the petitioner from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,02,893/- (Rupees Three lakhs two thousand eight hundred and ninety three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

(SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.5210/2021 The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Hanumantharaju vs Sridevi B. Math on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98360407/
6 Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
